UNIVERSAL.changelog:
Version 0.0.108 — updates that fail are caught, and uptime means something

An update is no longer treated as proven the moment it finishes starting. The
board now waits until the new version has been running for two minutes before it
stands down the rollback protection, so a version that starts cleanly and then
dies is still rolled back — which is the case the protection exists for. It also
refuses to stand down while an update is installed but not yet running, so the
protection is not spent on the version being replaced.

A board whose pixel driver firmware was left in the wrong place by an older
update now repairs itself at startup instead of refusing to start. That fault
could not be fixed by updating again, because the update that misplaced the
files was the one already installed.

Uptime is the daemon's own, everywhere it is reported. The status pages counted
from the first time anything asked rather than from startup, so a board running
for a week reported no uptime to whoever looked first — and the uptime announced
to other JBoards was the machine's, which does not change when the board's
software restarts. Both now report how long this board's software has actually
been running, which is what tells you whether it restarted.

Fleet updates verify what a board is running rather than what was copied onto
it, and send a restart request in the form the board accepts. Together these
made an update of another board report success while that board carried on
running its previous version.
